item.title: Ukraine Says Restrictions on Starlink Speed Have Been Lifted
item.description: Ukraine recorded no limits of the speed of its SpaceX Starlink terminal connections in overnight testing, a person familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Daryna Krasnolutska

item.title: France on Edge as New Protests Raise Fears of Violence, Looting
item.description: A new round of protests is set to hit France Saturday, raising fears of a repeat of last weekend’s riots.
item.dc:creator: Samy Adghirni

item.title: Kim Jong Un Visits China for Second Trip in Just Over a Year
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un arrived in the Chinese city of Dandong, his second visit in just over a year and before US President Donald Trump travels to the region next month.
item.dc:creator: Hooyeon Kim and Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Andy Burnham Tests Labour Loyalty With Budget Built for Bond Market
item.description: Next week, UK Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey must deliver what his predecessor, Rachel Reeves, couldn’t: A budget that keeps both the bond market and the governing Labour Party happy.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham, Chloe Chaplain and Joe Mayes

item.title: Serbian Vote Pits Putin-Backed Strongman Against Student Dissent
item.description: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic is mimicking his ally Vladimir Putin’s plan to extend his grip on power. He wants to swap the presidency for the prime minister’s job.
item.dc:creator: Misha Savic

item.title: Australian Lawmaker Who Lost Legs After Alleged Attack is Stable
item.description: An Australian lawmaker whose legs were amputated after she was struck by a car in an alleged attack outside her office in rural Victoria is in stable condition, according to hospital authorities.
item.dc:creator: David Stringer

item.title: Wall Street Week | Europe’s AI Player, Argentina’s Two Economies
item.description: This week, campaign costs are soaring, but democratic fundraiser Blair Effron of Centerview Partners says many races may already have reached the point where more money stops making much difference. And, even though most Americans dislike the proliferation of data centers, one community has welcomed them with open arms. Plus, the key difference Mistral hopes will set it apart in the global AI race. Later, Argentina President Milei brought inflation down and investment up, but its led to a fragmented economy one year out from an election. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Pushes DOJ Lawsuit Over Alaska Senate Race
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Gen. Ben Hodges (Ret.) says restrictions on Starlink service have dealt a significant blow to Ukraine's counter-drone capabilities and disrupted an early-warning system for incoming ballistic missiles. Carlos Gutierrez, former Commerce Secretary and CEO of Kellogg and author of Sheer Will, says trade under the Trump administration has become all-encompassing and can be used as part of geopolitical and political negotiations beyond trade itself. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gutierrez: US Has Gone Too Far With Tariffs
item.description: Carlos Gutierrez, former Commerce Secretary and CEO of Kellogg and author of Sheer Will, says trade under the Trump administration has become all-encompassing and can be used as part of geopolitical and political negotiations beyond trade itself. Gutierrez says the US has gone too far with tariffs and that easing them could help reduce inflationary pressure on American consumers. Gutierrez says the US has the infrastructure and capabilities to be a strong exporter, but should focus on high-value industries rather than making consumers pay more to bring back lower-value production. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gen. Hodges (Ret.) Says Trump Actions Help Russia's War
item.description: Gen. Ben Hodges (Ret.) says restrictions on Starlink service have dealt a significant blow to Ukraine's counter-drone capabilities and disrupted an early-warning system for incoming ballistic missiles. Hodges says it is bizarre for President Donald Trump to defend Elon Musk as a "good person" who would not do anything wrong, pointing to Trump's praise of Vladimir Putin and Kim Jong Un and comments from a Trump negotiator calling Putin a humanitarian. Hodges says he applauds first lady Melania Trump's role in helping secure relief for Ukrainian civilians, but says it represents only a small fraction of the suffering caused by Russia's war. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gen Z Investors Trim Portfolio Risks Ahead of Midterm Elections
item.description: Bloomberg's Zijia Song joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." Nearly three-quarters of Gen Z investors — those younger than age 30 — said they have switched up their portfolios ahead of the November US midterm elections, or were considering such a move. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Teneo’s Kajiwara on Market Positioning Amid Midterms
item.description: Kevin Kajiwara, Co-President of Political Risk Advisory at Teneo, says the market impact of the coming midterm elections will depend partly on how contentious they are. He identifies affordability as a central issue, linking tariffs and wars to higher fuel costs, while noting that rising interest rates and worsening fiscal conditions are also weighing on the outlook. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Blackstone Chips Bet (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Blackstone tactical opportunities group led a $2.3B private credit loan to CoreWeave in 2023, marking the first major deal of its kind and becoming a blueprint for chip-backed debt. This marked the first major deal of its kind and became a blueprint for chip-backed debt that, three years on, is on track to become a trillion-dollar market, eclipsing even the borrowings used to build the data centers housing the chips. It’s a testament to how intertwined the global AI expansion and credit markets have become in such a short time
On today's episode:
Dina Bass, Bloomberg News AI Infrastructure Reporter Jay Chaudhry, CEO & Founder, Zscaler Ray Madoff, Author, The Second Estate Jessica Dupuy, Co-Author of Italianity, Award-Winning Wine, Spirits, Food & Travel Writer (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What Investors Want to Know About Trump and the Midterm Elections
item.description: Looking at historical returns offers some clues.
item.dc:creator: Nathan R Dean

item.title: Big Take: Benjamin Netanyahu’s Referendum Has Finally Arrived
item.description: For the first time since the October 7 attacks, Israelis are headed to the polls. The race is seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is neck-and-neck with opponent Gadi Eisenkot in the latest polls. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stocks Fall as Oil Rally Keeps a Lid on Treasuries
item.description: A resurgence in oil prices dragged down stocks and bonds, stoking concerns about inflation just days ahead of the next Fed decision. Brent crude topped $116 as a flare-up in Middle East violence threatened global supply. The S&P 500 saw back-to-back losses, even as selling pressure on tech firms abated. Yields rose after the market’s best day in more than a year. Joe Weisenthal, Bloomberg ‘Odd Lots’ Podcast Co-Host, joins to wrap up the week in markets ahead of the next Fed decision and more tech earnings. Jayati Bharadwaj, Head of FX Strategy at TD Securities, weighs in on a rush to safe haven trades. Plus, Bloomberg News AI Infrastructure Reporter Dina Bass joins to discuss her reporting on Blackstone's bet on chips driving a debt boom. Finally, Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry on internet security in light of new PHP vulnerabilities across the web. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Names Stir Michigan Senate Race
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the latest from the White House. On today's show, Redwave Communications Owner David Kochel, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Friday Reporter Public Affairs Founder Lisa Camooso Miller and The States Project Co-Founder Daniel Squadron. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Changes Some Canada Tariffs in Bid to Aid Maine Senator
item.description: The Trump administration is expanding tariff exemptions to more Canadian products, a move that may help boost Republican Senator Susan Collins’ reelection campaign in Maine.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis, Josh Wingrove and Greg Ryan

item.title: Trump Steps Up Support for Ramaswamy Ad Despite GOP Blowback
item.description: President Donald Trump stepped up his support for a controversial ad featuring the estranged mother of Ohio’s Democratic candidate for governor, Amy Acton, despite intensifying Republican opposition to the campaign spot.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Trump, UK’s Burnham Set for Call as Tensions Rise Over Ukraine, Iran Policy
item.description: President Donald Trump spoke with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday as tensions build between the two governments over Russia’s war in Ukraine and the possibility of renewed US escalation against Iran.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain, Josh Wingrove and Alex Wickham
